question: Which methods exist for evaluating open-ended foundation models automatically, how do they work, and where do they fail?
contributions: Explains language modeling metrics (entropy, cross entropy, BPC, BPB, perplexity) and their uses.
Separates exact evaluation (functional correctness, exact/lexical/semantic similarity) from subjective evaluation (AI as a judge).
Lays out AI judge usage, limitations and biases, and comparative evaluation with rating algorithms.

limits: Many figures date from 2023 to 2024 (Chatbot Arena January 2024, tool criteria as of September 2024); built-in judge criteria are said to change as tools evolve.
The author concedes AI judge criteria are not standardized and judges change over time, so scores are not comparable across tools or versions.
Perplexity is a poor proxy for post-trained (SFT, RLHF) or quantized models.
Comparative evaluation says which model is better, not whether it is good enough; transitivity of preference is unverified.
Whether a weaker model can judge a stronger one is described as an open question.

The chapter reports others' numbers; it runs no experiment of its own beyond a GitHub repo count (over 50 evaluation repos among the top 1,000, May 2024) and a Chatbot Arena ranking analysis described but not shown.
practices: Do not trust any AI judge whose model and prompt you cannot see (Limitations, Criteria ambiguity).
State in the judge prompt the task, the criteria and the scoring system, and include examples per score (How to Use AI as a Judge).
Prefer classification over numerical scoring, and narrow discrete ranges (1 to 5) over continuous or wide ones (TIP, How to Use AI as a Judge).
Mitigate first-position bias by repeating tests with different orderings (Biases of AI as a judge).
Reduce judge cost by using weaker judges or spot-checking a subset of responses (Increased costs and latency).
Supplement AI judges with exact evaluation and/or human evaluation (Biases; Summary).
Use perplexity to detect data contamination, deduplicate training data, and detect abnormal text (Perplexity Interpretation and Use Cases).
Use functional correctness (pass@k with unit tests) wherever the task allows it (Functional Correctness).
Do not answer by preference questions that should be answered by correctness (Ranking Models with Comparative Evaluation).
Prefer a matching algorithm that samples matches reducing the most ranking uncertainty (Scalability bottlenecks).
Identify where the system is likely to fail and design evaluation around those places (chapter introduction).

terms.definition: Entropy measures how much information, on average, a token carries.
Perplexity is the exponential of entropy and cross entropy.
the number of bits a language model needs to represent one byte of the original training data
evaluating a system based on whether it performs the intended functionality
the fraction of the solved problems out of all problems, where a problem is solved if any of k generated samples passes all its test cases
Metrics that require references are reference-based, and metrics that don't are reference-free.
the generated response matches one of the reference responses exactly
measures how much two texts overlap
computes the similarity in semantics, by comparing embeddings (e.g. cosine similarity)
The approach of using AI to evaluate AI is called AI as a judge or LLM as a judge.
a model favors its own responses over the responses generated by other models
